heroText: Athens is a layered capital where ancient ruins, dense neighbourhoods and rooftop views sit under the Acropolis. Start at the Acropolis and Plaka, visit the Acropolis Museum, then use Monastiraki or Syntagma as anchors for food and transport. Athens International Airport connects by metro, suburban rail, buses and taxis.

areas.name: Plaka
areas.text: Plaka is the classic first base, with old lanes, restaurants and easy walks to the Acropolis.

areas.name: Syntagma
areas.text: Syntagma is practical for metro, airport links, shopping and quick access to central sights.

areas.name: Monastiraki
areas.text: Monastiraki is lively and central, with markets, rooftop bars and strong metro connections.

areas.name: Koukaki
areas.text: Koukaki is calmer, close to the Acropolis Museum and good for apartment stays.

airports.name: Athens International Airport (ATH)
airports.text: Athens International Airport is east of the city, connected by metro, suburban rail, express buses and taxis.

airportTransfer.value: 40-60 min by metro, bus or taxi to central Athens
airportTransfer.distance: about 33 km east of the centre

stayOverview: Plaka is best for a first historic stay, Syntagma for transport, Monastiraki for markets and nightlife, and Koukaki for calmer apartment stays near the Acropolis Museum.
hotelIntro: Athens is hot and hilly, so location matters. Stay near metro and the sights you care about most, then use taxis or transit for longer cross-city moves.
rentalCars: Do not rent for Athens; use a car only when leaving for mainland archaeology sites or beaches.
